title: It is not what you were told.
description:
It is not what you were told. The mantis shrimp is famous for seeing colours you cannot imagine. In 2014 someone tested what it can actually tell apart.

Eight across the range you can see, four more in the ultraviolet. You have three. Four is already enough for fine colour discrimination.

It is worse at this than you are. It could only separate wavelengths fifteen to twenty-five nanometres apart. You manage five. So do honeybees.

Working in Justin Marshall's lab in Queensland, she found the eye may not compare colours at all. It scans, and matches the reading against something like a lookup table.

It is not seeing more. It is seeing faster.
